wordmark.purpose: The masthead. Serif, tight, like a paper's name. One per shell.

figure.purpose: The hero figure: the one number the screen is about. One per screen, in crimson.

container-label.purpose: A statistic in a column of statistics (Apps / App data / Media).

section.purpose: Section headings, serif, set like a magazine's.

amount.purpose: The value at the end of a row. Playfair, like every other figure in the app.

stencil.purpose: Small tracked caps: the only sans voice that shouts. Buttons, text actions, risk words, field labels. Never a kicker.

title-large.purpose: Finding, notice and app titles. Playfair bold.

body-large.purpose: Tab words and category row labels.

body-medium.purpose: Plain-language detail under a title; stat labels.

motion.name: tab-tint
motion.purpose: The active tab's colour easing between pencil grey and crimson.

motion.name: tab-rule
motion.purpose: The 2dp underline fading in and out. The rule is always drawn; only its alpha animates, so column widths never shift.

motion.name: approval-bar-enter
motion.purpose: The approval bar rising from the bottom edge when the plan becomes non-empty.

motion.name: approval-bar-exit
motion.purpose: The approval bar leaving when the plan empties.

narrative.overview:
Tidyra is set, not laid out. The screen behaves like a page in a well-printed broadsheet: warm paper ground, a high-contrast serif carrying the wordmark and every number, generous margins, and hairline rules doing the structural work that cards, boxes and shadows do in a stock Material app. Nothing is enclosed. Sections are separated by a 1px rule and air, the way a printed page separates them.

The category this app sits in — Android "boosters" — is loud, gauged and rocket-animated, and it exaggerates findings for a living. The answer here is typographic authority instead of urgency: one crimson accent used sparingly, exact figures rather than rounded reassurance, and no illustration, no gauge, no donut chart, no mascot. Dynamic colour is deliberately switched off; a wallpaper-derived scheme would replace crimson with something arbitrary and the page would lose its one voice.

Density is reading density. A row is at least 48dp because a finger needs it, but the vertical rhythm is set by one 8dp module and the type carries the hierarchy. Dark mode is the same page printed on near-black stock: the same rules, the same rhythm, a lighter crimson so the accent still measures.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, never pure white; near-black ink, never pure black.
Playfair Display for the wordmark, every heading and every figure.
One crimson accent, read from the theme, never hardcoded.
Hairline rules and space instead of cards, borders and elevation.
Exact sizes, always — 756 MB, <1%, never a rounded 0%.
Marks are drawn on a Canvas at one stroke ratio; no glyph ever stands in for an icon.

rules.name: The Theme-Read Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent is always read from MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary, never from the Crimson constant. Hardcoding it once ran dark mode at the light value and measured roughly 3.2:1 against the night ground. If a composable names a crimson, it is a bug.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Crimson is the only accent. Olive and amber are 6dp status pips and never expand into surfaces, text colours or fills. Dynamic/wallpaper colour is off by construction.

rules.name: The Measured Colour Rule
rules.body: A colour earns its value by contrast measurement against its own ground, at the smallest size it is used on. The tracked 11sp caps are the governing case.

rules.name: The Playfair Figure Rule
rules.body: Every quantity in the app — hero figure, stat, row amount, percentage — is set in Playfair through StationType.amount or a larger serif role. A number in the sans face is a number that escaped the system.

rules.name: The Exact Figure Rule
rules.body: Sizes are formatted through Format and nowhere else: one decimal at GB scale, none below it, an em dash for unknown, and <1% for anything real but under one percent. A cleaner that says "about 0.7 GB" where it means 756 MB is rounding in its own favour. Every figure also has a spoken form (Format.spokenSize) so TalkBack reads "756 megabytes", not letters.

rules.name: The Stencil-Is-An-Action Rule
rules.body: Tracked 11sp caps mean "this is a control or a status tag" — button labels, SCAN, BACK, SAFE, SELECTED. They are never used as a kicker or an eyebrow above a heading.

rules.name: The 8dp Module Rule
rules.body: Every gap is a multiple of 8dp, with 4dp as the half-step. The only exceptions are Material's interactive minimums. Nothing sits off-grid "just this once".

rules.name: The One Margin Rule
rules.body: 24dp, both sides, every screen. A section that indents differently from the masthead breaks the page.

rules.name: The Status Bar Ownership Rule
rules.body: Exactly one composable in any stack owns statusBarsPadding() — the masthead in the tabbed shell, the detail host on a detail screen. Never both.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is made of 1px rules and space. If a region needs to be set apart, give it a rule and a margin — not a card, not a border box, not a shadow.

rules.name: The No-Enclosure Rule
rules.body: Nothing in this app is enclosed in a container. A card is the wrong gesture on a printed page.

rules.name: The Stable Tab Weight Rule
rules.body: A tab's font weight never changes with state. Bold text is wider; an active tab would resize and shove every other tab along the row. Colour and the underline carry state. Nothing else does.

rules.name: The One Denominator Rule
rules.body: Every quantity drawn anywhere in the app — a category share, a finding, the span a plan would free — is drawn through SizeScale against the device's total capacity, and is never re-normalised per screen. A megabyte is the same visual length everywhere. A real but tiny quantity still gets a visible sliver (floor 0.4%), capped so the floor can never make something look larger than the next real value up.

rules.name: The Counted-Once Rule
rules.body: A file that belongs to two findings is counted once in the plan, and the overlap is stated on the row rather than quietly resolved. Totals across findings must reconcile with the approval bar.

rules.name: The Drawn Mark Rule
rules.body: No Unicode glyph, icon font or vector pack ever stands in for an icon. A glyph borrowed from the text font is not an icon: set in Playfair, an arrow arrives as a thin double chevron at the font's weight and matches nothing else on the page. A new mark is authored in Marks.kt at the same stroke ratio or it does not ship.

dos: Do read the accent from MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary in every composable.
Do set every quantity in Playfair, through StationType.amount or a larger serif role.
Do format every size and percentage through Format, and give every figure a spokenSize for TalkBack.
Do draw every bar through SizeScale against the device's total capacity.
Do keep every gap on the 8dp module, with 4dp as the only half-step.
Do separate with a 1px rule and 24dp margins.
Do author new marks in Marks.kt at the 0.12 stroke ratio.
Do give a tappable row at least 48dp and a selection control a full interactive target.
Do let exactly one composable in a stack own statusBarsPadding().
Do state an overlap on the row when a finding shares items with another.
donts: Don't hardcode Crimson or any other palette constant in a composable; it breaks dark mode's contrast.
Don't enable dynamic colour. Crimson is the only accent.
Don't put a quantity on a per-screen or per-row axis; there is one denominator.
Don't round a size for comfort, and never print 0% for something that exists.
Don't add a shadow, an elevation or a card. Rules and space carry structure.
Don't change a tab's font weight, or any text's weight, to signal state.
Don't use a Unicode glyph, icon font or vector pack as an icon.
Don't add ripple to a text tab.
Don't add statusBarsPadding() to a section rendered under the masthead.
Don't let a corner radius exceed 4dp outside the circular selection controls and status pips.
